newsitem.title: USA: NRC proposes fine for Wolf Creek Kan. nuke.
newsitem.headline: NRC proposes fine for Wolf Creek Kan. nuke.

text.p: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Friday it has proposed a $100,000 civil penalty against Wolf Creek Nuclear Operating Corp for violations at the 1,200 megawatt Wolf Creek nuclear power plant.
The violations were identified during NRC inspections conducted last October, the NRC said in a statement.

The violations included five instances in which Wolf Creek failed to identify and correct conflicts between technical specifications and written interpretations of those specifications prepared by plant officials, the NRC said.
Another violation involved the unauthorized change of technical specifications concerning the frequency of testing for reactor coolant pump flywheels, the NRC said.
Wolf Creek Nuclear Operating Corp said in a separate statement that none of the violations resulted in an unsafe plant condition.
Wolf Creek said it anticipates paying the fine once the proposed enforcement action has been reviewed in detail.
The Wolf Creek nuclear plant is located in Kansas.
Wolf Creek is a subsidiary of Kansas City Power & Light Co.
